notes:
Lead profile: small martech vendor building SaaS for mid-market e-comm and agencies.

Use case summary:
- Primary: high-volume marketing content generation (email bodies, ad copy, social snippets).
- Secondary: automated SEO meta generation for customer sites and batch summarization for briefs.

Requirements / constraints (from calls):
- Very cost-sensitive: CFO looking for unit economics before committing. Goal: keep cost/token effectively < $0.0009 on avg.
- Throughput: bursts of 200-300 requests/min during campaigns; typical steady-state ~20-50 rps.
- Latency target for UI generation: 200-500ms (acceptable up to 800ms for long copy).
- Prefer public cloud hosted API (self-serve). Not ready for Dedicated or Private.
- Interested in built-in caching (prefix + KV) and auto-batching suggestions to lower per-token cost. Asked specifically: "Can you show a config that drops cost by 30% using batching + caching?"
- Model preferences: open, cost-effective small-medium models for bulk ops; preservation of higher-quality variants for paid-tier customers. Want routing/fallback to cheaper variants when load spikes.
- Security: SOC2 is required by some customers; SSO/SAML for their admin console; audit logging for content generation events. No strict data residency needs today.

POC ask / technical notes:
- They want a 2-week trial with 100k token/day cap to emulate campaign traffic.
- Devs requested examples: batching strategy (max batch size, timeout heuristics), prefix caching examples for repeated prompts, and metric dashboard screenshots for token/latency breakdown.
- Provided sample prompt patterns and token distribution (attached in Drive).

Conversation excerpts / quotes:
- "We need predictable unit costs — if we can't forecast campaign spend we can't sell to agencies." — Head of Product.
- "Show me a simple batching config I can paste into our worker." — Senior Backend Eng.

Next steps (PRIORITY):
1) Send hosted trial invite + default batching/caching config (Marina) — DONE 2026-03-05.
2) SE (Daniel) to prepare a 30m POC call with engineering to walk through sample configs and run a small live burst test (target week of 2026-03-15).
3) Share one-pager on retention controls & audit logging for SOC2 reviewers (attach to Drive).

Potential blockers: budget sign-off from CFO; SAML integration timeline (they use Okta, want estimate for setup); visibility into long-run cost before scaling.

CRM style notes: short, fragmented, prioritize actions. Follow-up cadence: weekly until POC complete.
